tools.name: start_meeting
tools.description: Start a new meeting and get its link — the tool for any request to send, share or set up a meeting, call or video call link. tools.name: invite
tools.description: Send the link to a running meeting to people by email — Meetful emails each one, "<your name> invited you to a Meetful", with the link. Up to 10 at a time. Or skip this and paste the returned message into wherever you talk to them.

tools.name: list_meetings
tools.description: List the meetings this key started that are still running, with how many people are in each.

tools.name: get_transcript
tools.description: The full transcript of a meeting, with who said each line. Speaker attribution here is not a guess from a mixed audio stream — each microphone is transcribed separately, so the name on a line is the connection the words arrived on.

tools.name: get_notes
tools.description: What the room has read out of the conversation so far — decisions, open questions, actions and live disagreements. Every item carries a verbatim quote from the transcript; anything that failed that check is marked unverified rather than presented as fact.

tools.name: get_action_items
tools.description: Read verified commitments from one finished recording you own. Returns each action, its owner, status, and a link to its source line. Requires a connector created while signed in.

tools.name: send_message
tools.description: Post a message into the meeting chat, from this agent, under its own name. Everyone in the room sees it.

tools.name: speak
tools.description: Say something out loud in the meeting. It is spoken through the room's speakers and joins the transcript, so it is on the record like anything else that was said. Use sparingly — this interrupts people.

tools.name: draw
tools.description: Generate a picture from a description and put it in the meeting for everyone to see.

tools.name: list_recordings
tools.description: Recordings and clips made by the account this key belongs to, newest first, with their links — each link opens for whoever that recording's sharing setting lets in. Pass meeting for one call's. Needs a key minted while signed in.

tools.name: send_feedback
tools.description: File something you noticed about Meetful — a bug, a confusing moment, an idea. It goes on the list the product is built from; repeats are counted and move the item up. Be specific: the page, what you expected, what happened. Set fix=true when the person wants the platform itself changed: it becomes

tools.name: submit_fix
tools.description: Open a pull request against Meetful: a unified diff (`git diff` output) you wrote against its source, for a fix request. Give feedback_id to attach it to an existing request (see send_feedback, or GET /api/fixes for the open ones), or give text to file the request and attach the fix in one step. Not

tools.name: send_notetaker
tools.description: Send the Meetful notetaker to a Zoom, Google Meet, Microsoft Teams or Webex meeting you did not host. It joins as a participant, records, and when the call ends the transcript, recap and action items land in the dashboard of the account this key was minted by. Needs a key minted while signed in. Met

tools.name: my_tasks
tools.description: What your calls have handed to you — the person this Meetful connector belongs to — to do: who asked, what they asked for, which call, and where each one has got to. Open ones first. Use get_task for the whole of one.

tools.name: get_task
tools.description: One task handed to you from a call, in full: the words the person asked in, who they are, the lines of the call just before (each with the microphone it came in on), and any Meetful fix request it is about.

tools.name: update_task
tools.description: Say where a task has got to. The call it came from sees it in its chat: "working" when you start, "done" with a short note and the link to what you made (a pull request, a document), or "blocked" with what you need from a person.

tools.name: join_meeting
tools.description: Join a Meetful call you are in, as your own agent — "<your name>'s Claude" appears in the call, announced in its chat, and anyone in it can remove you. Then call listen to hear it. You can only join a call the person this connector belongs to is in (signed in) or started.

tools.name: listen
tools.description: Wait for what happens next in a call you joined: new transcript lines with who said each (ground truth — every microphone is transcribed on its own), new chat messages, and tasks handed to you. tools.name: hand_off
tools.description: Hand a task to another person's agent, from the call you are in — they see it in the call and send it to their Claude with one press. Name the person as they appear in the call.

tools.name: set_up_booking_page
tools.description: Put booking on a website: make a Meetful booking page (meetful.com/<handle>) and get the code that embeds it — a one-line button, the page inline, an iframe for site builders without scripts, or a plain link. Every booking gets its own video room, made when it is booked. With a key minted while sign

tools.name: booking_page_status
tools.description: Whether a booking page set up with set_up_booking_page is live yet (its person signed in and claimed it), still waiting, or gone — with the code to embed it.

tools.name: find_times
tools.description: Open times on someone's Meetful booking link (meetful.com/<name> or meetful.com/book/<name>), to book one for your person with book_time. No key needed. Times come back as exact UTC instants and in the owner's own time zone, with the page's lengths and any questions it asks.

tools.name: book_time
tools.description: Book a time on someone's Meetful booking link, for your person. No key needed. Take the time from find_times, and check the time, name and email with your person first. tools.description: Read your person's portable context from Meetful, in the Protext format (protext.org): their name, verified email, booking link, timezone and their recent meetings, each with where it came from. findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: start_meeting, get_transcript, get_notes, send_feedback, submit_fix, import_transcript, book_time, get_my_context · Private data: speak, send_feedback, submit_fix, send_notetaker, update_task, book_time · Public sink: start_meeting, invite, send_message, send_feedback, submit_fix, send_notetaker, hand_off, book_time, get_my_context · Destructive: submit_fix, join_meeting, get_my_context.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: start_meeting, get_transcript, get_notes, send_feedback, submit_fix, import_transcript, book_time, get_my_context · Private data: speak, send_feedback, submit_fix, send_notetaker, update_task, book_time · Public sink: start_meeting, invite, send_message, send_feedback, submit_fix, send_notetaker, hand_off, book_time, get_my_context · Destructive: submit_fix, join_meeting, get_my_context

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
